"""Reduction from Hamiltonian Cycle to Hamiltonian Path.

Given an undirected graph G = (V, E) we construct a graph G' as follows:

   s – u … (a – b) … v – t
where the middle part is a Hamiltonian path from u to v in the original graph
(with the edge (u, v) deleted).  Adding the deleted edge (u, v) closes this
path into a Hamiltonian *cycle* in G.  Conversely, any Hamiltonian cycle in G
contains the edge (u, v); deleting it yields a Hamiltonian u‑v path, which can be
extended with the new vertices and edges to a Hamiltonian path in G'.

Thus G has a Hamiltonian cycle iff G' has a Hamiltonian path.  The construction
runs in linear time.

    """Reduce a Hamiltonian‑Cycle instance to a Hamiltonian‑Path instance.
